$comment: The words for /jobs/ and /companies/<id>/ (docs/design/jobs-board.md), from the marketing session. Pay lines are checked against the game: change them if its numbers change. kinds: haulage, starter, contractor, rush, survey, assignment, coming-soon, build (Wexley-Yorozu's design commissions: not contracts on the board).

hexon.imageAlt: A wireframe Coriolis station in orbit above a glowing planet
hexon.pitch: Join a company that cares. Continuously. Hexon Holdings carries the medicine, the luxuries and the sealed containers that keep the safe core safe. We pay well and on time, and we expect the same of you.
hexon.ground: The safe core: Corporate States, Democracies and Confederacies.
hexon.empty: Nothing from Hexon Holdings at Lave {when}. Hexon prefers the safe core: {station}, {jumps} away, is its ground.

card.sub: Continuity of care. A company in a free browser game.

hexon.description: Hexon Holdings, a fictional company in Witchspace, the free browser space game: medicine, luxuries and sealed containers. Curiosity discouraged.

vorg.imageAlt: A pirate dogfight in orange and violet laser fire
vorg.pitch: Vorg Industries makes hulls, lasers, alloys and pest control, and moves them wherever the law has given up. The work is dangerous, so the pay is too. Most of our pilots come back.
vorg.speech: “They told me nobody would fly to the frontier. Nobody would carry freight where the law is thin. Nobody would buy a hull rebuilt from three others. They were right about nobody. They were wrong about you.”
vorg.speechCite: Aurelius Vorg, from his annual address (abridged; the original runs to four hours)
vorg.cardLine: Danger pay included. Pirates also included.
vorg.ground: The frontier: Anarchies, Feudal worlds and Multi-Governments.
vorg.empty: Nothing from Vorg at Lave {when}: it works the frontier. {station}, {gov} {jumps} away, is its ground.

card.sub: We build. You survive. A company in a free browser game.

vorg.description: Vorg Industries, a fictional company in Witchspace, the free browser space game: frontier freight, danger pay, and crates that tick.

mutual.imageAlt: A Cobra Mk III resting in its berth in a station hangar
mutual.pitch: Twenty-eight captains, a station bar, and three rules: share the risk, share the work, and come when called. One member, one ship, one vote. The pay is fair, the meetings are long, and someone always comes.
mutual.ground: A little of everywhere with a government.
mutual.empty: Nothing from the Mutual at Lave {when}. The members are probably in a meeting. Try {station}, {jumps} away.

card.sub: No hauler flies alone. A company in a free browser game.

mutual.description: The Carriers' Mutual, a fictional co-operative in Witchspace, the free browser space game: fair rates, honest freight, and someone always comes.

wy.imageAlt: A rift in space, its rim bright white against the stars
wy.pitch: We build the atmosphere processors, the stations and the ships that turn poisoned rock into home. Over half the work on Lave's board is ours, and our Science Division is always interested in what you find out there. Our colonies are free to join. The terms are on page 214.
wy.cardLine: Long routes, steady work. Mind the paperwork.
wy.surveyLine: No cargo. Look closely, and tell us first.
wy.ground: Thinly settled worlds with moons to build from.
wy.empty: Nothing from Wexley-Yorozu at Lave {when}, which is unusual: it posts over half the work here. Try the next board.

card.sub: Better worlds, built to order. A company in a free browser game.

wy.description: Wexley-Yorozu, a fictional company in Witchspace, the free browser space game: colony supply, moon surveys and stations built to order.

adverts.title: Discreet Medical Courier
adverts.text: Carry medical supplies between Corporate States and Democracies. Punctuality essential. Curiosity discouraged.
adverts.meta: Safe core · Supplied cargo · Typically 50 to 250 Cr a run

adverts.title: Luxury Goods Haulier
adverts.text: Fine wines, luxuries and computers for discerning worlds. You will be trusted with valuable cargo once we trust you.
adverts.meta: Contractor standing · Bigger loads, typically 300 to 1,000 Cr

adverts.title: Specimen Transport Associate
adverts.text: Sealed class-4 biologicals, by invitation only. No prior biology required. No later biology permitted.
adverts.meta: By invitation · 600 Cr and up · Do not open

adverts.title: Frontier Freight Pilot
adverts.text: Alloys, machinery and minerals through Anarchies and Feudal worlds. Big danger bonuses. Pirates included at no extra charge.
adverts.meta: The frontier · Supplied cargo · Typically 50 to 250 Cr, danger pay included

adverts.title: Irregular Cargo Specialist
adverts.text: Some of our crates tick. Applicants must not mind ticking, ask about ticking, or report ticking to the police.
adverts.meta: By invitation · 600 Cr and up · Questions not answered

adverts.title: Pest Control Operative
adverts.text: Our pest control division answers Thargoid incursions very quickly. Some say before. Apply now to find out.

adverts.title: Member-Haulier
adverts.text: Food, textiles, water and furs, wherever there's a government and a need. The friendliest first job in the galaxy.
adverts.meta: Almost everywhere · Supplied cargo · Fair rates, typically 50 to 250 Cr

adverts.title: Relief Runner
adverts.text: When a member is stranded with sick crew, someone has to get there first. The treasurer always finds the money.
adverts.meta: By invitation · 600 Cr and up · Remembered

adverts.title: Junior Haulier, Lave
adverts.text: Most of the work on Lave's board is ours. Food, textiles, furs, water and liquor: whatever Lave exports, wherever it's short. Three to sixteen tonnes: every load fits an empty Cobra. Start the moment you dock.
adverts.meta: Lave · Supplied cargo · Open to new pilots

adverts.title: Colony Supply Pilot
adverts.text: Machinery, electronics and medicine for frontier colonies with moons to build from. Long routes, steady work.
adverts.meta: Thinly settled worlds · Supplied cargo · Typically 50 to 250 Cr a run

adverts.title: Rush Freight Pilot
adverts.text: A yard is waiting and so are we. Rush jobs pay 40 % over the usual rate, in fewer jumps. Late still pays half. We will mention it.
adverts.meta: Rush · Supplied cargo · 40 % over the usual rate

adverts.title: Survey Contractor
adverts.text: Fly out to a system's moons, take a close look, and hand the data in at any Wexley-Yorozu station. No cargo. No customs. No questions about why we want them.
adverts.meta: Moons · No cargo needed · From about 350 Cr, more per moon

adverts.title: Science Division Courier
adverts.text: Special orders, delivered intact. Crew safety is a secondary consideration.
adverts.meta: By invitation · 600 Cr and up · See clause 214

adverts.title: Module Designer, Titanoboa
adverts.text: Design a section of our constructor to the coupling standard: a greenhouse, an ice refinery, a chapel, a racing gate for the workers' day off. If we build it, we pay the commander whose callsign is on the design, and put that callsign in the catalogue. The design becomes the property of Wexley-Yorozu in perpetuity, across all systems known and unknown.* The company thanks you for your contribution.
adverts.meta: Build · 5,000 Cr when it's first fitted · Designed by you

adverts.title: Module Improver
adverts.text: Make one of our modules better: a cleaner shape, a better place for the docks. If we accept it, your callsign goes on the module beside its designer's. Small fixes are welcome, but only better modules are paid.
adverts.meta: Build · 2,000 Cr when it's first fitted · Revised by you

adverts.title: Detention Module, open brief
adverts.text: The Co-operative Marshals need somewhere to keep what they catch. A block of cells, one clear shape, and nothing facing the crew that shouldn't. Standard commission applies.
adverts.meta: Build · Open brief · 5,000 Cr when it's first fitted

adverts.title: Hull Designer, Fleet Office
adverts.text: Our freighters reach every system on time, to the timetable. They also all look the same. Design us a working hull: a bulk freighter, a liner, a tug, a mining ship. One clear shape you'd know at ten kilometres, built to carry, not to fight. An accepted hull flies in company colours across the galaxy, with your callsign in the registry. The design becomes the property of Wexley-Yorozu in perpetuity, across all systems known and unknown.* The Fleet Office thanks you for your patience.
adverts.meta: Build · Open brief · Your callsign in the registry
adverts.note: No drawing board? Ask your own AI assistant. [Add the Witchspace connector (space.witchspace.org.uk/mcp)](/get-involved/#ai) and it checks your hull against the Fleet Office standard and draws it beside a Cobra.

adverts.title: Regulars Wanted, the Saloon
adverts.text: Every Mutual station keeps one chair empty. Help us fill the others. Write us a regular: who they are, what they want, and where their ship goes when they're not at the bar. A smuggler who drinks on Mondays and runs dark on Thursdays. A captain who never forgave Hexon. Write them well enough and they'll be out there, keeping their own hours, and remembering who helped them. The members will vote on it. Slowly.
adverts.meta: Build · Writing · On the ideas board

howItWorks: The company supplies the cargo. You fly it there.
Deadlines are counted in hyperspace jumps, so closing your browser never makes you late.
Deliver well and your standing rises, which opens bigger work. At Contractor, the companies start getting in touch.
start: Every commander starts at Lave in a Cobra Mk III with 20 t of hold and 100 Cr.

jobs.description: Jobs in Witchspace, a free space game in your browser: the live contracts board at Lave, from four fictional companies. Paid in credits. No CV.

card.sub: The live board at Lave. A free game in your browser.

build.intro: Wexley-Yorozu commissions designs: sections of the Titan, its constructor ship, and the working hulls that fly its routes. The Carriers' Mutual wants writers for the people in its Saloons. These aren't contracts on the board. You design something, and if it's accepted, it's in everyone's game. Module commissions also pay your commander, in the game.
build.note: *In the game. Out here, you keep your copyright: designs are shared under CC BY-SA 4.0, like the rest of Witchspace. Paid in credits, in the game, to the signed-in commander whose callsign is on the design. Nobody is paid real money. The real reward is your name on it and your module flying in everyone's game.
build.how: Hand it in on Hand in a design: no GitHub needed, and it's checked as you go. The standard is on the design page. A pull request on GitHub works too. Just an idea? Put it on the ideas board.
